meta.title: Chimney Tuckpointing & Masonry Repair Toronto | Northmark
meta.description: Chimney tuckpointing, masonry repair and rebuilds in Toronto & the GTA. Repointing, brick replacement and crown work matched to your home. Free inspection.

hero.p: Toronto freeze-thaw is hard on brick. We repoint worn joints, replace damaged brick, repair crowns and rebuild above the roofline when it comes to that — matched as closely as possible to your home’s original brick.
hero.t-2: Joints cut out and repointed — not smeared over
hero.t-4: From one joint — to a rebuild above the roofline

signs.h2: Signs Your Chimney Masonry Needs Work
signs.p: Brick and mortar tell you when water is getting in.
signs.p-2: Mortar wears out first, by design. Open joints let water in behind the brick.
signs.p-3: Spalling — frost pushing the face off the brick. It keeps going once it starts.
signs.p-4: Salt left behind as water moves through the masonry.
signs.p-5: The slab on top is the chimney’s roof. Cracks send water straight down inside.
signs.p-6: Above the roofline the weather is hardest, so that is where it shows first.
signs.p-7: Not sure which one you’re seeing? That is what the free inspection is for. Book it here or call {{site.phone}}.

inc.h2: From A Joint To A Rebuild
inc.p: Chimney masonry is not one job. These are the four scopes we work in, smallest to largest — the free inspection tells you which one your chimney is in.
inc.p-2: The joints are worn or open but the brick is sound. We cut the old mortar out to a proper depth and repoint it, matching the colour and joint profile.
inc.p-3: The most common masonry job, and the one that prevents the expensive ones.
inc.p-4: When the crown cracks, water runs straight down inside the chimney. Small cracks can be sealed; a broken crown is cut out and recast with a proper overhang and drip edge.
inc.p-5: Fixing a crown early is the cheapest way to avoid a rebuild.
inc.p-6: Where frost has pushed the face off individual bricks, those bricks come out and matching ones go in. The rest of the chimney stays where it is.
inc.p-7: Worth doing while the damage is counted in bricks, not in courses.
inc.p-8: When enough of the structure has gone — usually above the roofline — we take it down to sound masonry and rebuild. Same brick where we can match it, new crown, new cap.
inc.p-9: The point of the other three jobs is to never need this one.

how.p: Every visit starts with protecting your home and ends with photos and a clean work area.
how.p-2: Failed joints ground out to sound depth; loose or spalled bricks removed.
how.p-4: Joints packed and struck to match the original profile — not smeared over the face.
how.p-5: Crown checked and, where it makes sense, breathable masonry waterproofing applied.

faq.p-2: Cutting back failing mortar joints and refilling them properly — struck to match the original profile, not smeared over the brick face.
faq.q-2: Can you match the brick on an older home?
faq.p-3: Matching is the craft. We source and blend as closely as possible so the repair blends into the original work.
faq.q-3: When is a rebuild needed instead of repair?
faq.p-4: When brick and joints have deteriorated past the point of repointing — usually above the roofline. The free inspection tells you honestly which side of that line you’re on.
faq.q-4: What season is best for masonry work?
faq.p-5: Mortar needs workable temperatures, so most masonry runs spring through fall. Book early — the season fills up.
faq.q-5: How much does masonry repair cost?
faq.p-6: It depends on the scope — a few joints or a rebuild — so we price it after the free inspection, at your home, before any work starts.
